findings.title: Stand-down leaves the capture context armed (openContext, lastSnapshot, _settleSince, sessionActive), so re-enabling records movements made while disabled
findings.evidence: NS.StandDown never clears these fields. A headless repro shows a deposit made while disabled written as 1 ledger row after re-enable at the same bank visit. Disabling at a bank, closing it and re-enabling elsewhere leaves openContext=BANK_FRAME, so every BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED or PLAYER_MONEY, in combat too, schedules a full rescan. That undercuts the performance-§12 exemption premise. sessionActive stays true, so later rows append to the old visit. None of the 11 test_disabled cases opens a storage context.
findings.remediation: C-01: add L:DropContext() in modules/Ledger.lua. It cancels the pending reconcile, nils openContext, lastSnapshot and _settleSince, and fires SessionChanged(false) if a context was open. Call it as step 3b inside NS.StandDown, before the bus targets are dropped. There is no second teardown path and no CloseContext flush. Add 2 test_disabled cases with red-under comments (1017 to 1019), regenerate docs/test-cases.md, move the badge, and update the ARCHITECTURE stand-down section. Smoke test C-01, cases A and B.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (What MUST stand down); performance-§6; performance-§12; testing-§12
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. NS.StandDown (core/BankLedger.lua:146-191) cancels timers, unregisters events, refreshes upvalues, drops the bus targets and hides windows, but it never touches NS.State.openContext, lastSnapshot, L._settleSince or State.sessionActive. The only paths that clear them are L:CloseContext (modules/Ledger.lua:803-815) and disarmGuildBankIfGone (:624-631), and both need events that are unregistered while disabled. L:Enable (:856-890) re-registers the CHANGE_EVENTS, and L:ScheduleReconcile (:670) only checks that openContext is set. So after a re-enable, the next BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED or PLAYER_MONEY diffs against the pre-disable baseline, or triggers full rescans away from the bank. The remediation is sound: DropContext before step 4 still reaches SessionWindow's __ev with SessionChanged(false), and skipping the flush is correct. Severity drops from high to medium. The trigger is narrow, because the player must disable while a bank frame is open. Away from the bank, a stale BANK_FRAME context mostly sees one-sided changes that settleBaseline re-anchors, not phantom rows. The real impact is movements from the disabled period being captured, needless rescans until the next bank open (which breaks the performance.md premise), and a session that never ends. None of that is data loss.

findings.title: 'Reset all settings' while disabled restores settings.enabled=true in the store but never re-runs the latch
findings.evidence: ResetEverything wipes db.global in place and merges defaults, bypassing the row onChange and NS.ReevaluateEnabled. Repro: stored enabled = true, IsDisabled = true, IsStoodDown = true. The checkbox says enabled while nothing records until /reload or a toggle. None of the 8 ResetEverything cases runs while disabled.
findings.remediation: C-02: after the SETTINGS_CHANGED send and before refreshAfterReset(), call NS.ReevaluateEnabled() (as OnProfileReset does). Add a test_panel case 'ResetEverything while disabled stands the addon back up' (+1). Behavior change: a reset made while disabled re-enables. Note it under API/behavior changes. Smoke test C-02. Coordinate with the BL-34 reset unification.
findings.rule_ref: options-ui-§12 (indistinguishable from a fresh install); slash-commands-§7 (re-evaluate when the stored switch can change)
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. Sl:ResetEverything (settings/Slash.lua:161-197) wipes db.global in place and merges defaults back, which restores settings.enabled=true (defaults/Global.lua:42). It then sends only SETTINGS_CHANGED 'reset' and calls refreshAfterReset (:119-131). Nothing calls NS.ReevaluateEnabled or NS.SetDisabledHold. The only callers are core/Database.lua:19 (profile callbacks, which never fire because there are no profiles), core/BankLedger.lua:69 (OnEnable) and the Schema row onChange (settings/Schema.lua:224), and the wipe bypasses that onChange. The panel and the reset button are setup surfaces, so they are reachable while disabled. The remediation to call NS.ReevaluateEnabled() after the reset is correct. Severity drops from high to medium. The trigger is rare (a full reset while the addon is disabled), and the effect is an addon that stays off while its checkbox says on. That means capture is silently lost until a /reload or a toggle, but no stored data is corrupted.

findings.title: Default 30-day retention silently deletes older history at login; the README never discloses it
findings.evidence: retentionDays = 30 by default. The prune runs once per session at login. The 164-line README and its FAQ never mention retention. The only disclosure is a dropdown tooltip on Settings > History.
findings.remediation: C-03: add a README FAQ row saying that movements older than 30 days are removed at login by default and can be kept under Settings > History > Keep history for, optionally with a note beside /bl purge. Changing the default to 0 is an optional owner decision (CP2). If taken, note that AceDB strips default-equal values, so players who deliberately chose 30 will also move to 'Always'. Record this under the Version History behavior changes. Drop the savedvariables-§1 rule citation, because this is a documentation (player-facing README) gap.
findings.verify_reason: The facts are accurate. retentionDays=30 is the default (defaults/Global.lua:47, settings/Schema.lua:118). PruneOld deletes older rows (core/Database.lua:656-675) through the once-per-session OnEnterWorld prune. README.md (164 lines) has no retention mention, and the only disclosure is the dropdown tooltip. Severity drops from medium to low. This is a deliberate default that the settings UI discloses, so the gap is in the player-facing documentation, not a code defect. The cited rule is also wrong: savedvariables-§1 is 'Structure' (the defaults table shape) and says nothing about retention. The finding rests on the README being player-facing, not on a standard MUST. The remediation also has a caveat: AceDB strips default-equal values, so a player who explicitly picked 30 while 30 was the default has nothing stored. Changing the default to 0 would silently flip that player to 'Always', so the owner decision should weigh that.

findings.title: The retention prune's C_Timer.After(5) survives the stand-down (gated, not cancelled), and the cleanupDone latch set before the timer skips the prune for the whole session
findings.locations: core/BankLedger.lua:216-229 (latch :218, C_Timer.After :220, IsStoodDown check :221-225); core/State.lua; docs/performance.md:47
findings.evidence: C_Timer.After cannot be cancelled. A disable within 5 s of the first loading screen leaves it armed, and its body finds a flag and returns. That is exactly the shape slash-commands-§7 forbids. Every other timer goes through AceTimer and StandDown's CancelAllTimers (:151-155). Because cleanupDone=true is set before the timer, retention is also skipped until the next session (review F-009).
findings.remediation: Audit (BL-46): schedule through NS.addon:ScheduleTimer(fn, 5) (or keep a C_Timer.NewTimer handle) so NS.StandDown cancels it. Keep the IsStoodDown belt, and clear cleanupDone on cancel or document the skip. Review (C-07): move the latch inside the timer with a session-only cleanupPending flag in core/State.lua, so a stand-down postpones rather than cancels. Retry on the next PEW. Combine the two: an AceTimer-armed prune plus the latch set only when the prune runs. Add a falsification case ('stand-down inside the prune window postpones rather than cancels'; red under C_Timer.After), +1 test. Update docs/performance.md:47. Smoke test C-07. Do this after R-06, the mock fix.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (every timer is canceled, not left armed to find a flag); testing-§12
findings.verify_reason: core/BankLedger.lua:216-229 sets NS.State.cleanupDone=true at :218, before the C_Timer.After(5) at :220, and the body only checks NS.IsStoodDown (:225). C_Timer.After returns no handle, so StandDown's CancelAllTimers (:151) cannot reach it. slash-commands-§7 'What MUST stand down' says every timer is canceled, 'not left armed to wake up and find a flag'. That is exactly this shape, and the comment at :221-224 concedes it. Setting the latch before the timer also means a disable inside the 5 s window skips retention for the rest of the session. The combined remediation (an AceTimer-scheduled prune, with the latch set only when the prune runs) is correct, and so is the docs/performance.md:47 update. Low severity fits.

findings.title: Five event registrations bypass the pcall-isolating helper; no C_EventUtils.IsEventValid front gate anywhere
findings.evidence: Only the capture engine uses L:RegisterEventSafely. In NS.StandUp, a raise on the first of the three registrations would also abort Ledger:Enable, Browser:Enable and SessionWindow:Enable. ARCHITECTURE's argument that the names cannot retire is prose, not the helper. The problem is latent.
findings.remediation: S3-3: promote to a shared NS.RegisterEventSafely(target, event, handler) (core/Util.lua or BankLedger.lua) writing one registered/unavailable record that /bl debug scan reports and NS.StandDown resets. Front-gate it with C_EventUtils.IsEventValid when available, keeping the pcall. Route all five sites through it. Add a test that a bad name in the stand-up block does not stop Ledger:Enable, and update the ARCHITECTURE Event Subscriptions section. Coordinate with R-08, whose PIM registration uses the same helper.
findings.verify_reason: core/BankLedger.lua:87,91,92 (NS.StandUp) call self:RegisterEvent directly, before Ledger/Browser/SessionWindow:Enable (:93-97). A raise there would skip all three Enables. modules/Browser.lua:1218 and modules/SessionWindow.lua:673 register PLAYER_LOGOUT directly. Only modules/Ledger.lua:849-854 L:RegisterEventSafely pcalls. events-frames-taint.md:30 is a MUST: every RegisterEvent goes through a single pcall'd helper. So this is a real MUST deviation with no register row. The names are long-lived, so the impact is latent and low is right. The IsEventValid front gate (:32) is a SHOULD aimed at names newer than supported clients, so it is optional polish for these names. The pcall promotion is the load-bearing part.
